title: Silas and the Playlist
premise: Paloma Winterbourne has survived seven years at Ashgrove Academy by being flawless and forgettable, until a teacher pairs her with Silas Reyes—the boy whose family the school destroyed—for a semester project on local history. Digging through archives, they uncover a playlist of recordings left by Silas's late aunt, a whistleblower whose death the board ruled an accident, and evidence that the academy's founding fortune was built on stolen land and silenced students. As the board moves to expel them and seal the records, Paloma must choose between her scholarship and the truth, broadcasting the playlist to the entire school during Founders' Day. The exposure forces resignations and a public reckoning, but justice comes at a cost: Paloma loses her place at Ashgrove, only to inherit something greater—her own voice, and a community that finally sees her.
about_author: V. M. Zhou is the pen name of a former boarding-school archivist who spent years cataloguing other people's secrets before writing her own. She lives near the coast, where she collects vinyl records and stories nobody meant to survive.

chapters.title: The Assignment
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Told to partner with Silas Reyes for a history project, Paloma panics—his aunt's death is the scandal no one names, and proximity means danger to her careful invisibility. Their first archive session is all friction and suspicion, until Silas finds his aunt's name redacted in a board minute. Emotional beat: reluctant alliance sparked by shared fury.

chapters.title: Side B
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. In a storage room, they discover a box of cassette tapes—Silas's aunt's voice documenting bribes, forged land deeds, and student complaints buried over decades. Listening together, grief turns to resolve. But a janitor reports them, and the headmaster issues a quiet warning. Emotional beat: intimacy through inherited pain; first taste of real fear.

chapters.title: Founders' Day Eve
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. The board fast-tracks their expulsion and schedules the archive demolition for after Founders' Day. Paloma proposes the impossible: hijack the ceremony's sound system and play everything. They spend the night digitizing tapes while security patrols close in, and Paloma confesses why she stayed silent so long. Emotional beat: terror transmuted into commitment; trust sealed.

chapters.title: Loudest Thing in the Room
chapters.summary: Both POVs. During Founders' Day, they splice the playlist into the anthem broadcast—the aunt's voice fills the quad as students stop mid-parade. Chaos, confrontation, and the board's collapse follow. Paloma accepts expulsion with her chin up; alumni and townspeople rally, forcing an independent inquiry. Epilogue beat: months later, a new plaque bears the aunt's name—and Paloma's.
